- Overestimate prices in early forecast windows, especially after recent spikes; reduce initial forecast values.
- Underestimate prices in late forecast windows; adjust upward if recent history shows sustained upward trend.
- Overshoot after sharp price spikes; cap forecast peaks at 10–15% below true peak or use moving average smoothing.
- Model tends to overreact to recent volatility; apply dampening factor to volatility-weighted components.
- Mean reversion bias: if forecast is >10% above recent 7-day average, reduce by 5–10% unless confirmed by strong fundamentals.
- Lagged response: if true outcome is >5% higher than 30-day history, forecast should be adjusted upward by 2–3% for next period.
- Avoid overfitting to recent 30-day history; use 7-day rolling average as baseline for correction.
